printed_headline_estimate: Spearman rank correlation rho = -0.521, p = 0.018 (printed as ρ = -0,521; p-valor = 0,018), N = 24 regional water/sanitation service providers offering social tariffs (summed from 4+6+5+3+4+2 providers using 1 to 6 criteria; PDF pp. 16-17, Section 4.3 & Figure 6), testing number of social-tariff eligibility criteria against % of CadÚnico low-income families (with water network access) receiving the social tariff. (All public-vs-private ownership contrasts in Tables 2-3 and Figures 2-4, 7-8 are descriptive only without inferential tests.)
publication_year_note: Primary journal volume/issue year ('Data do Fascículo' and 'Como citar', PDF pp. 3, 22, 27) is 2025 (urbe. Revista Brasileira de Gestão Urbana, v. 17, e20240258, 2025; received 20 Oct 2024, accepted 02 Jul 2025). SciELO collection posting date ('Publicação nesta coleção', PDF p. 27) is 12 Jan 2026, and the e-locator carries submission-year prefix e20240258.
rationale: Although the paper's comparisons of public vs. private ownership and regional vs. local service delivery models (Sections 3.1, 4.2, 4.4; Tables 2-3) are explicitly descriptive percentages, medians, and means without hypothesis tests or uncertainty estimates, Sections 2.3 (p. 9) and 4.3 (pp. 16-17) report a statistically significant inferential Spearman rank correlation (ρ = -0.521, p = 0.018, N = 24 regional utilities) linking a narrow rule-type tariff/administrative-hurdle exposure—the number of cumulative eligibility criteria required for social-tariff enrollment—to a household water economic-access/exclusion outcome—the percentage of low-income CadÚnico-registered families with piped water access who actually receive the social water tariff. Higher administrative/eligibility criteria counts significantly reduce low-income beneficiary coverage, fitting SWiM Family C (tariffs, regulation, and administrative rules).
